data.body:
## OPERATOR DECISION: option (a) — Windows IS to be a declared support target

The operator has chosen **(a)**. Windows becomes a declared support target, so this ticket
converts from "a permanently-red job is not a signal" into the seed of a **portability epic**.

This is the larger of the two paths and it is a sustained commitment, so recording the shape
precisely matters.

## What this decision changes about the job itself

`sweep (windows)` currently runs with `continue-on-error: true` and the comment "Windows is not
yet a declared support target, so a genuine incompatibility is a visible finding, never a red
gate." **That comment is now false** and must be revised as part of the epic.

But the job must NOT simply be flipped to gating on day one: it would redden every change
immediately with 510 failures that have nothing to do with the change under review, which would
destroy the Verified signal rather than improve it. The gating flip belongs at the END of the
epic, as the criterion that proves the epic is done. Until then it stays informational — but now
as a KNOWN-INCOMPLETE support target being driven to green, not as a permanent red badge nobody
intends to fix. That distinction should be visible in the tree.

## The decomposition, ordered

From the failure census on this ticket: 510 failed, 5140 passed, 69 skipped, 74 errors across 115
distinct test files.

**FIRST, and it gates everything else — `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (377 of 510, 74%).**
`lock.py:72-75` guards the fcntl IMPORT but not its USE, at `lock.py:207` (`_acquire_fcntl`) and
`lock.py:254` (`write_lock_is_busy`). Every store write reaches `_acquire_once` -> `_acquire_fcntl`
(`lock.py:491`), so on Windows every ticket write raises
`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'`.

**THE OBVIOUS TWO-LINE FIX IS UNSAFE AND MUST NOT BE TAKEN.** Skipping the fcntl leg when
`fcntl is None` silently breaks a documented, load-bearing invariant: `_acquire_mkdir`
(`lock.py:325-362`) passes `fcntl_held=True` into stale-lock reclamation, and its docstring states
the precondition — reclamation is race-safe ONLY because an exclusive `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` was
already taken, so a live owner could not be there. Degrade to mkdir-only and `fcntl_held=True`
becomes a lie: rebar would reclaim a write lock held by a LIVE process. That is silent store
corruption under concurrency, which is worse than not supporting Windows at all.

A correct fix needs a real alternative exclusive leg (`msvcrt.locking` / `LockFileEx`) AND a
rework of the staleness proof. AC5 stands: no change may weaken the `fcntl_held=True` precondition
without replacing the exclusivity proof it depends on, and a test must fail if that invariant is
degraded. Note that sibling modules already guard correctly
(`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:79`, `_snapshot/janitor.py:430`, `reducer/marker.py:33`), which is why
`lock.py` is an outlier rather than a deliberate design choice.

**THEN, the remaining ~133 failures — independent platform semantics, not one shared cause.**
Each is its own child, and each must name its own proving command (AC3):
- POSIX mode-bit assertions
- CRLF translation
- the cp1252 console codec
- `os.path.relpath` across `C:` / `D:` drives
- `.EXE` console-script invocation
- a network guard that leaks on Windows

**PLUS an ADR** recording the support-target decision and its consequences — this is now a
portability commitment that binds future work, and the blocking `project.portability` plan-review
criterion will be read against it.

## Acceptance criteria, as they now apply

AC1 (disposition recorded with reasoning) is satisfied in part by this comment but belongs in the
tree — the ADR is where it lands. AC3 becomes the operative one: the epic exists with per-class
children, `lock.py` first, each child naming its own proving command. AC4 is satisfied by fixing
`lock.py` properly rather than documenting it as a limitation, since the limitation is no longer
acceptable under (a). AC5 is unchanged and is the guardrail on the whole first workstream.

AC2 (the (b) branch — remove the permanently-red entry) drops away, superseded: the entry stays,
but its meaning changes from "ignorable" to "tracked and being driven to green".

## Next step

Decomposition into the epic has NOT yet been done. That is the immediate follow-on and should
produce: the ADR, the epic, and per-class children in dependency order with `lock.py` first.
